question.text: A beam of unpolarised light of intensity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is passed through a polaroid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and then through another polaroid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> which is oriented so that its principal plane makes an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> relative to that of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>. The intensity of emergent light is :

solution.text:
Intensity of polarised light from polaroid A will be I02. Therefore,

Intensity of emergent light
=I02cos245°=I04
